title: Accounts Manager
description:
Account Manager Accountancy Practice

Location: Somerset (office-based across two local offices)
Job Type: Permanent Part-Time (up to 40 hours per week)
Salary: £35,000 £40,000 FTE (depending on experience)

A well-established and growing accountancy practice is looking to recruit an experienced Account Manager to join its friendly and supportive team.

This is a fantastic opportunity for an experienced practice accountant who enjoys working closely with a varied client portfolio and is looking for a role offering flexibility, autonomy, and long-term career stability.

The Role

You'll be responsible for managing a portfolio of clients, ensuring a high standard of service across accounts preparation, bookkeeping, VAT, payroll, and general compliance. This is a varied role where you'll build strong client relationships while supporting businesses with their day-to-day accounting requirements.

The successful candidate will have the flexibility to spread their hours across two local offices and should be comfortable travelling between sites when required.

Key Responsibilities
- Managing a portfolio of clients across a range of industries.
- Preparing management accounts, year-end accounts, and financial reports.
- Completing bookkeeping, bank reconciliations, and maintaining accurate accounting records.
- Preparing and submitting VAT returns in line with HMRC requirements.
- Supporting payroll processing where required.
- Managing accounts payable and receivable.
- Assisting with year-end compliance and liaising with senior colleagues where necessary.
- Building and maintaining strong client relationships, acting as a key point of contact.
- Supporting clients with accounting software and day-to-day finance queries.
- Ensuring compliance with accounting standards and HMRC regulations.
- Identifying opportunities to improve internal processes and client service.

About You

The ideal candidate will have:
- ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent professional qualification.
- A minimum of three years' post-qualified experience within an accountancy practice.
- Experience preparing statutory accounts, VAT returns, payroll, self-assessment tax returns, and limited company accounts.
- Strong working knowledge of cloud accounting software such as Xero, QuickBooks, Sage, or similar.
- Excellent organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple deadlines.
- Strong communication and client relationship skills.
- A proactive and professional approach with excellent attention to detail.
- The ability to travel between two local office locations as required.

What's on Offer
- Salary of £35,000 £40,000 FTE, depending on experience.
- Flexible part-time hours (up to 40 hours per week).
- Friendly and supportive working environment.
- Health and wellbeing initiatives.
- Company events.
- Long-term opportunity within a respected and growing accountancy practice.

If you're an experienced practice accountant looking for a varied client-facing role with flexibility and genuine career stability, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Senior Accounts Technician
description:
A growing accountancy practice is looking to recruit a Senior Accounts Techncian into their Weston-Super-Mare office providing year end accounts, tax and wider service provision to a varied industry client base. You will gain increasing responsibility and technical skill development as you progress within this firm and role.

Client Details

Based in Weston-Super-Mare this accountancy practice acts for a wide ranging and varied client base of sole traders, partnerships, limited company OMBs, SMEs, not for profit/charity and other clients of varying sectors and turnover size. As a result of ongoing growth an opportunity is available for the right Senior Accounts Technician to join the team with excellent benefits, hybrid working, full or part time hours along with competitive salary on offer.

Description

You will join the team as a Senior Accounts Technician where you will take responsibility for the hands on provision of year end accounts preparation, tax, personal and corporate, VAT, bookkeeping and other services to a wide spectrum of clients. Alongside providing a quality compliance service, you will have opportunity for increasing client contact and responsibility looking to build relationships with clients. You will prepare accounts/ tax and provide other services for sole traders , limited companies and partnerships, corporate and personal tax along with other responsibilities . Given the growth in the business and structure of the firm, you will have opportunity to carve a long term career move, with a clear development and progression path on offer, along with full study support for those pursuing qualifications.

Profile

You may be AAT qualified/studying or have developed your career entirely through experience only to date, or be pursuing ACCA/ACA. You will have a background working within the accountancy practice sector specifically as an Accounts Technician / Senior Accountant, or similar level, Accounts and Tax Senior, experienced Semi - Senior etc. You will bring a mix, or any of year end accounts preparation, tax, bookkeeping, VAT etc and be looking for a new challenging career move, where you can see a clear route to progress within a successful team and firm. Study support on offer.

Job Offer

£26,000 - £30,000 + dependent on background and experience, all to be explored. Please apply online and for a further confidential discussion to find out more please contact Mark Bailey on .

title: Medical Records Co-Ordinator, St Georges
description:
Medical Records Co-ordinator Advert

Mendip Vale Medical Group

Salary: £12.90 per hour Hours: 20 hours per week, worked over Thursday and Friday

About the role

We're looking for a methodical, detail-focused Medical Records Co-ordinator to join our records team. This is a largely administrative role, with the great majority of your time spent on accurate, independent processing work rather than direct patient contact, so it suits someone who's happy getting their head down and working through detailed tasks without needing a highly social or fast-changing environment.

You'll be joining a close, established team of 11, with a good mix of experience levels, including colleagues who've been with us a long time alongside others who value the flexible part-time hours.

What you'll be doing
- Updating and maintaining patient medical records, from registering new patients through to deactivating records when they leave
- Handling patient requests to access their own medical records
- Supporting authorised access requests from insurance companies
- Reading, coding and accurately logging correspondence, both paper and electronic
- Using anatomical and physiological knowledge to apply the correct codes and link related information on a patient's record
- Keeping all patient files and related admin to the required quality standards, in line with information governance, GDPR and DPA regulations

What we're looking for

Essential:
- GCSE English and Maths at grade C or above (or equivalent experience), plus evidence of ongoing personal development
- Medical terminology and coding experience
- Experience working within an NHS environment relevant to accurate data recording
- Good general IT skills, including Word, Excel, email and databases
- Able to prioritise and manage competing demands while hitting deadlines
- Tact and sensitivity, with the ability to build trust and confidence
- Strong, adaptable communication across different audiences
- Patient-focused, compassionate, resilient and flexible

Desirable:
- NVQ3 in Administration (or working towards)
- Experience implementing service improvements involving clinical data
- Experience using GP clinical systems such as EMIS
- Understanding of medical terminology and basic anatomy and physiology
- Self-directed, calm under pressure, positive, and a strong team player

Why join us
- A steady, focused role well suited to someone who prefers independent, detail-driven work over a highly social or patient-facing environment
- A supportive, experienced team, with colleagues on hand to help you learn the systems
- Fixed, predictable hours over Thursday and Friday, working well alongside other commitments

Mendip Vale Medical Group is committed to equality and diversity, and welcomes applications from all backgrounds.

You will then be contacted by one of our specialist consultants, who will provide you with further details about the role.
If you would like to talk ahead of sending us your CV, please give us a call on (phone number removed). Please note, any contact is in the strictest confidence and we will not send your details to any practice without your expressed consent to do so.
Is this role almost right for you, but not quite ticking all the boxes? If so, we have hundreds of other roles available and can also work proactively to find you your perfect post.
We have been named as the Recruitment Firm of the year at the HealthInvestor Awards, Winners of the Professional Service Provider of the Year at the General Practice Awards, Winners of the Recruitment Award at the LaingBuisson Awards and named on the Recruiter Hot 100 list, so in dealing with us you ll be in safe hands!

title: Patient Co-ordinator, St Georges
description:
Patient Co-ordinator, St Georges, Weston-Super-Mare

Progressive GP Group of Practices

Looking for a career that matters?

Every day, thousands of patients contact the practices in this large, innovative group looking for help, advice and support.

As a Patient Co-ordinator, you'll be the first person they speak to.

You'll listen, guide, reassure and help patients access the right healthcare professional or service. It's a role where your communication skills, empathy and ability to stay calm under pressure can genuinely make a difference to someone's day.

No healthcare experience? No problem.

We can teach you the systems. We can teach you the processes. You will already have developed transferrable skills and qualities in your career to date.

If you're personable, organised, reliable and enjoy helping others, we'd love to hear from you.

Why join this group?

We're one of the largest and most innovative group of GP practices in the South West, caring for more than 85,000 patients across 10 sites throughout Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire.

We've invested heavily in our people, systems and facilities, creating modern working environments and a supportive culture where people can build long-term careers.

What you can expect:
- Detailed training from day one
- Structured induction and ongoing support
- Weekly one-to-one meetings during probation
- Monday Friday working pattern to include:

Monday full day, Wednesday afternoon and Friday full day
- Supportive team environment
- Opportunities for career progression
- Continuous learning and development

A career, not just a job

Many of our Patient Co-ordinators go on to develop their careers within the organisation.

Previous team members have progressed into Medical Secretary, Healthcare Assistant and management positions. One former Patient Co-ordinator even progressed into an HCA role before going on to study Medicine.

If you're ambitious and eager to learn, we'll support your development every step of the way.

What you'll be doing

As a Patient Co-ordinator, you'll be at the heart of our patient services team.

You'll:
- Be the first point of contact for patients contacting the practice
- Help patients access the most appropriate healthcare service
- Manage appointment requests and bookings
- Provide excellent customer service both over the phone and face-to-face
- Support patients with enquiries and administrative requests
- Create and maintain accurate patient records
- Process correspondence and documentation
- Work closely with GPs, nurses and other healthcare professionals
- Help ensure patients receive a safe, efficient and positive experience
- Every day is different, and every interaction matters.

Hours

25.5 hours Monday full day, Wednesday afternoon, Friday full day

What we're looking for

You don't need healthcare experience.

We're particularly interested in hearing from people with customer service backgrounds in:
- Retail
- Hospitality
- Customer service
- Reception
- Contact centres
- Front-of-house roles

You'll be:
- A confident communicator
- Comfortable speaking with people on the phone
- Compassionate and patient-focused
- Organised and able to manage multiple tasks
- Comfortable using computers, email and Microsoft Office
- Calm under pressure
- Keen to learn and develop

Essential
- GCSE English and Maths (or equivalent experience)
- Experience in a customer-facing role
- Strong communication skills
- Commitment to delivering excellent service

Desirable
- Experience within a GP surgery or healthcare setting
- Knowledge of EMIS or patient record systems
- Administration experience

What our team says

"No one expects you to know everything when you start. The training and support are fantastic, and there's always someone willing to help."

At this group of GP practices, you'll join a team that genuinely cares about patients and each other.

Ready to make a difference?

If you're looking for a rewarding role where you can help people every day, learn new skills and build a long-term career, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today and become part of a team that puts patients first.

PLEASE NOTE, this is not a VISA sponsoring employer. Applicants are required to be eligible to work in the UK for the long term. (5 years+)
Kirsty Morris

title: Medical Receptionist
description: The Crown Medical Centre is a busy GP practice in Taunton, caring for a patient population of approximately 10,000 patients. Our team includes GP partners, salaried GPs, nurses, healthcare assistants and a wider administrative and clinical team. We are looking to recruit an enthusiastic, friendly and motivated Medical Receptionist to join our reception team. The successful candidate will be one of the first points of contact for patients contacting or visiting the practice. We are looking for someone with excellent communication and customer service skills who can provide a welcoming, professional and efficient service to our patients. This is a busy and varied role, requiring someone who can remain calm under pressure, use their initiative and work effectively as part of a team. Previous GP reception experience would be desirable but is not essential, as training will be provided. The hours for this vacancy are 22 hours per week, with the following working pattern: Monday: 12:30-18:30 Tuesday:12:00-17:00 Wednesday: 12:00-17:00 Thursday:12:30-18:30 Applicants should be able to commit to these hours. However, we may be able to consider slight adjustments to the working times for the right candidate, subject to the needs of the practice. Interview arrangements: We anticipate holding interviews during the first week of December 2026. The date will be confirmed with shortlisted candidates. The main responsibilities of the role will include: Acting as the first point of contact for patients attending or contacting the practice. Answering incoming telephone calls and dealing with patient enquiries in a professional and courteous manner. Greeting patients and visitors and directing them appropriately. Booking, amending and cancelling appointments in accordance with practice procedures. Processing prescription requests and home visit requests in line with practice protocols. Passing messages and information accurately to the appropriate members of the clinical or administrative team. Dealing with patient queries and providing information about practice services and procedures. Maintaining accurate patient information and records using the practice's clinical computer system. Ensuring patient confidentiality is maintained at all times. Keeping the reception and waiting areas tidy and welcoming. Undertaking other reasonable reception and administrative duties as required. Responsible to: Reception Supervisor / Deputy Practice Manager Job purpose To provide a professional first point of contact for patients and act as a central point of communication between patients, clinicians and the wider primary healthcare team. Main duties and responsibilities Record patient arrivals on EMIS Web and direct patients to the appropriate consulting or treatment room. Use practice signposting and reception protocols to direct patients to the most appropriate service. Manage patients without appointments who require urgent advice in accordance with practice protocols, escalating concerns to a clinician or appropriate team when necessary. Process new patient registrations, check the reception email inbox daily and confirm patients reside within the practice catchment area. Explain practice arrangements and requirements to new and temporary patients, ensuring registration procedures are completed accurately. Take payments for private services and issue receipts in accordance with practice procedures, referring concerns to the secretarial team. Respond to patient and visitor enquiries professionally and promptly. Add home visit requests to the Urgent Care Team for review. Check the NHS 111 list regularly and ensure relevant patients are transferred to the Urgent Care Team for same-day GP review. Manage laboratory results received by telephone promptly and in accordance with practice protocols. Record patient signposting accurately using the appropriate EMIS Web template. Review incoming online consultation requests and process them in line with practice protocols, directing them to the appropriate clinician or service and escalating where necessary. Maintain familiarity with the appointment system, including routine and ad hoc changes. Book appointments in accordance with practice policy, seeking guidance from the Reception Supervisor when required. Ensure patient details on EMIS Web are accurate and up to date, including address, contact details and personal information. Receive and make telephone calls, transfer or divert calls appropriately, and ensure telephone systems are operational at the start of the day and switched to the out-of-hours service at the end of the day. Maintain a clean, tidy and welcoming reception and waiting area. Respond to spillages or bodily fluids in accordance with infection prevention and control procedures, including the safe use of spill kits where required. Complete a clear end-of-shift handover, communicating outstanding tasks, unresolved issues and relevant information to incoming staff. Receive and check deliveries, signing for items as required. Ensure vaccines are recorded in the appropriate log, passed promptly to the nursing team and stored correctly. Forward invoices and delivery notes to the Deputy Practice Manager. Notify relevant staff of deliveries and ensure prescription paper deliveries are reported to the Prescriptions Team for logging and secure storage. To act as a chaperone during patient consultations or examinations when required, in accordance with the practice's Chaperone Policy. The post-holder must undertake any required training and follow the practice's procedures to ensure patient dignity, privacy and confidentiality are maintained. Inform the Deputy Practice Manager of damage, faulty equipment, complaints and other issues requiring attention. Undertake other reasonable duties in accordance with the needs of the practice. Understand and maintain strict confidentiality in accordance with information governance standards. Undertake and maintain appropriate safeguarding training.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: We are looking for friendly, organised and enthusiastic Receptionists to join our team at Penn Hill Surgery. Process payments for private (non-NHS) services, issue receipts and maintain accurate financial records. Work closely with clinical and administrative colleagues to ensure the smooth day-to-day running of the practice and deliver excellent patient care. Medical records summarising MEDICAL RECEPTIONIST Hours: We welcome applications from candidates who would be available to work within our core hours: Vacancy 1 : Tuesday 8:30 - 6:00, Thursday 8:30 - 6:30, Friday 8:30 - 6:00 Total hours: 27.25 Vacancy 2 : Wednesday 8:30 - 6:30, Thursday 8:30 - 5:30, Friday 8:30 - 6:30 Total hours 27.00 Place of Work: Penn Hill Surgery Reports to: Deputy Practice Manager Job Summary We are looking for friendly, organised and enthusiastic individuals to join our hardworking and supportive Reception Team. We have increased the hours in the reception team in order to provide greater variety in the day-to-day administrative duties, creating a rewarding role that combines reception responsibilities with a range of administrative tasks. Reception is at the heart of our practice and is often the first point of contact for our patients. This is a busy, fast-paced role where no two days are the same. The successful candidates will enjoy working with people, be able to manage a variety of competing demands, remain calm under pressure and provide a professional, compassionate service to our patients. Whether you have previous experience working in general practice or are looking for a new challenge, we will provide the training and support needed to help you develop in the role. You will work closely with our clinical and administrative teams to ensure patients receive the highest standard of care while contributing to the smooth running of the practice. Main Responsibilities Reception Provide a professional, friendly and efficient reception service to patients, visitors and healthcare professionals. Answer telephone calls, deal with general enquiries and signpost patients to the most appropriate clinician or service. Book, amend and cancel appointments using practice systems. Use your judgement and communication skills to ensure patients requiring urgent medical attention are managed appropriately in accordance with practice procedures. Explain practice services, registration procedures and temporary patient arrangements. Maintain accurate patient records using EMIS. Check and update patient demographic details as required. Process payments for private (non-NHS) services and issue receipts. Administration As well as reception duties, you'll also undertake a variety of administrative tasks, including: Actioning tasks received via EMIS, AskMyGP and email. Processing new patient registrations, temporary registrations and deductions. Scanning and coding clinical correspondence onto patients' electronic records. Supporting the wider practice team with general administrative duties to help ensure the smooth running of the practice. Summarising patient medical records. Premises Prepare the surgery for the start of the working day. Secure the premises at the end of the day when required, ensuring practice procedures are followed. General Responsibilities Attend team meetings, staff meetings and mandatory training. Participate in service improvement initiatives. Maintain confidentiality at all times in accordance with GDPR, NHS guidance and Practice policies. Work flexibly and undertake other duties appropriate to the role as requested by the Partners or Management Team.

title: Medical Records Clerk
description: Somerset NHS Foundation Trust is looking to recruit a Medical Records Clerk (Band 2) to join our busy Medical Records Department based in Priorswood. This is a practical, hands on role suited to someone who is organised, reliable and enjoys working in a fast paced environment. Retrieve, prepare and distribute patient case notes in line with clinic schedules and urgent requests Create new medical records and ensure no duplicate records are generated File, track and return records accurately using electronic tracking systems Identify missing, duplicate or damaged case notes and escalate issues appropriately Answer telephone enquiries and respond to emergency record requests Maintain confidentiality and comply with Information Governance and Records Management policies Support the safe, secure and efficient running of the Medical Records Department Assist with mentoring and supporting new team members as required Please refer to the attached Job Description and Person Specification for more information about the role.
